page: Microsoft Azure D160alds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The instance provides 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 80 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 320.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and instruction set extensions covering AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA extensions. There are no discrete GPUs attached.

Integrated local storage comprises 9448 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, providing direct fast storage alongside Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Synthetic and system benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded throughput, reaching 287,625.19 in stress-ng multi-core and 29,391.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached read and write memory bandwidth measure 463.49 GB/sec and 209.95 GB/sec respectively. PassMark results record 145,894.28 on the CPU score and 41,687.71 on database operations.

The 2.0 GB per core configuration trades expansive per-thread memory capacity for high parallel compute and rapid local NVMe throughput. The server suits highly parallel computational workloads, software compilation pipelines, large-scale Redis in-memory caching deployments capable of high request volumes, batch compression jobs, and high-concurrency static web serving.
